prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1349; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the policyholder's driver regarding a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has provided the vehicle and policy information requested so far.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the loss. Nothing in the policy file or the vehicle history suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report and spoke with the responding officer, who confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. No independent witnesses were identified, so the account rests on the claimant's statement and the available photos.

Entry 4: Photos of the rear bumper, trunk area, and tail lamp assembly are consistent with the impact described. The visible damage pattern matches the reported collision, and no prior damage to the vehicle is known from the records reviewed.

Entry 5: Claimant reports neck and back strain and has been treating for somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. The injury is consistent in kind and force with the crash as described, and no earlier injury to the same body areas is known from the records checked.

Entry 6: The claimant has given the same account of the collision in each conversation so far. Claim remains open pending review of the treatment records and the repair estimate.
